title: A viewer on another machine shows a server over the network
body:
dmabufs cannot cross a network, so a remote viewer needs the server's frames encoded, sent, and decoded, over decade's own protocol.

## Open

- Encoding: the GPU's video encoder, lossless updates of changed regions, or a mix. Video codecs blur fine text.
- Transport and latency over a link such as Tailscale.
- Mapping macOS keys, Cmd to Super in particular, to the server's keyboard.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/575e4e76
notes.text:
The review of the viewer protocol spec on 2026-11-07 left these for the remote step:

- Heartbeats, so a viewer and a server notice a dead link.
- Timestamps taken when the server receives input, since clocks differ across machines.
- Server-side key repeat that keeps going when a key-up arrives late over the network.
- Remote clipboard transfers. Locally they go through a pipe fd, which cannot cross a network, so remote needs data messages with flow control.

These input kinds are missing from version 1 for every viewer, local or remote: pointer lock and relative motion, touch, gestures, tablets, IME and text input, and drag and drop between the host and panes.
